doc.title: Wayne Bergeron interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 29, 2020

title: Day job at McDonnell Douglas and leaving to tour with Buddy Miles
summary: After high school the gigs dried up, he dropped out of college and worked at an aircraft plant before getting a call to go on the road with Buddy Miles.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: Day jobs: musicians working outside music

blocks.x: bucks and we’d play weddings on the weekends. So now all of a sudden I’m doing a couple of gigs and making 150 bucks on the weekends in the 70s. And I was like, man, I’ve made it, man. I never flipped burgers, or I never did any of that. Now I did do some other day jobs. I worked as a machinist because my father was a machinist. So the day jobs I took were those things. Then as I started playing I kind of made some money, you know, through high school, and I got to where I could drive eventually and of course could drive myself to the gigs. But then I thought well this is how it goes, and I’ve made it. Then when high school ended and some of these bands stopped working and I decided to go off to college and I’m going I’m not making any money, I’m not really practicing, I’m not really taking the trumpet very seriously. So I took a day job at McDonnell Douglas Aircraft, which is Boeing now, but, in Long Beach, because I needed a job. And I dropped out of school and I took this day job. And I barely played. I played on the weekends every once in a while one of these bands would have a gig and I would play, but it was kind of a rude awakening because nobody really groomed me for what you need to do to actually make a living playing music. You know you’re not just going to play in a wedding band and make a living. You know what I mean? That’s not going to happen. There’s a variety of things you have to do, no matter where you live, and Los Angeles is an entertainment town here you know so it’s one of the few places you can make a living as just a musician, you know if you’re fortunate enough to be with the right crowd. So you know I would do several different things. You know it took me a long time, as I said how I got in the business, but it took many years, you know, for me to get into it. I ended up quitting the day job. I did get a chance to go on the road with this guy Buddy Miles.
So I worked at the day job for one year, then I got a call to go on the road, so I took that. I said I want to go on the road. I was living with my parents at the time.
